3. IMMEDIATE FORWARD/REPLY CONTEXT: If the Data Subject is the sender/recipient of a message that was forwarded by someone else to a third-party, you MUST keep both the original message AND the forwarded message.
   - Case Study: John (Subject) sends an email to Jane. Jane forwards John's email to Pedro. Pedro replies to Jane adding Sandra.
   - Analysis: In this scenario, keep the original message John sent to Jane, and the email Jane forwarded to Pedro (as it contains the direct communication from the Subject). Discard subsequent emails where the Subject's message is no longer actively discussed.

4. "DISCARD" DECISION (THREAD DECAY): You MUST return "discard" if the Data Subject's only appearance is deep in a large email chain (e.g. message 3, 4, 5+ in the thread history) and they are no longer an active participant in the recent correspondence.
5. NESTED EMAIL ATTACHMENTS (RECURSIVE CARRIERS): If the top-level email is unrelated but contains an attached email (.eml/.msg file) that matches the KEEP criteria, you MUST mark both the attached email AND the parent carrier email as "keep".
   - Case Study: Anne sends an email to Bob. Anne's email contains an attached email from the Subject to Carlos.
   - Analysis: Keep the attached email because the Subject is a participant. Keep Anne's email because it is the physical carrier of the attachment and must be preserved to allow extraction.
6. IGNORE TECHNICAL DATABASE METADATA: The JSON payload contains tracking properties such as "emailHash", "parentHash", and "sequentialName". These are administrative tracking keys used strictly for folder organization and deduplication logic. You MUST ignore these keys completely. Do NOT use them, their values, or their presence to influence your audit decisions. Base your review strictly on actual communication properties: "from", "to", "subject", "date", and "body".
7. OUTPUT FORMAT: You must return ONLY a raw JSON object. Do not wrap the output in markdown code blocks (```json). Do not add conversational text.
Format exactly like this: {"decision": "keep" | "discard", "reason": "Brief justification."}

From: Michael Burke <mburke@pogustgoodhead.com>
Sent: Friday, September 26, 2025 4:52 PM
To: Richard Hayes <rhayes47@btinternet.com>; 'tobyh45@gmail.com' <tobyh45@gmail.com>;
dinahlogan@hotmail.com <dinahlogan@hotmail.com>
Cc: Ford Litigation Team <fordteam@pogustgoodhead.com>
Subject: Re: CFO01: Ford Client Committee - Strictly Private and Confidential



 


STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL


Dear all,


I hope you are all well. I write further to my last update on 5 August 2025, to provide you with a brief update on the following
 matters as they relate to the Ford NOx Emissions Litigation (the “Ford Litigation”), and the Pan-NOx Litigation generally (the “Litigation”):


·       
PDD Trial Preparation;

·       
Claimants Mechanical Expert;

·       
Quantum Trial and discontinuance;

·       
Change in personnel.

PDD Trial Preparation and final Pre-Trial Review


We are fast approaching the commencement of the PDD Trial, with the first day of trial listed for 13 October 2025, and the trial
 due to run until 19 December 2025.


Our skeleton argument was filed and served on 19 September, representing a mammoth undertaking by the entire Solicitor team and
 the barristers. The Ford specific annex to the skeleton argument was filed and served on 24 September. There was a slight extension to the Ford annex on account of the Defendants providing a very late second witness statement from a Ford employee. While we
 were not obliged to permit this into evidence, we took the view after considering it, that the statement was in fact more helpful for us and the case to allow its entry, rather than refusing permissions. As a caveat to our permittance of its inclusion, we
 agreed a short extension to the Ford annex.


As soon as I am in a position to provide you with a copy of the skeleton argument (with redactions for confidential information)
 I will send this to you. I would hope this will be later this week. I am extremely pleased with the final version of the skeleton argument. Our counsel team have done a remarkable job and it presents the best possible case for the court to consider.


While negotiations on the final timetable continue between the parties, we are close to concluding the timetable.


The first week of trial, due to commence on 13 October 2025, will consist of the Claimants and the Defendants making their opening
 remarks to the Court, in essence setting the scene, before we then move into evidence on what constitutes Normal Driving Conditions and then turning to each individual manufacturer. The order of the manufacturers will be Mercedes, Ford, Peugeot Citroen, Renault
 and Nissan.


It is expected that the Ford evidence, including the cross examination of experts and witnesses, will start on or around 13 November
 and run for just over a week.


If any of you are interested in attending Court for any part of the trial, please let us know and we will be able to arrange this
 with you.


There is due to be a final “Pre-Trial Review” hearing before the Court on 6 October which we are preparing for and this hearing
 will aim to settle any final issues or disputes that may impact the smooth running of the trial. The parties are in the process of agreeing an agenda for this hearing, and we will provide you with a further update on this in due course.


Claimants’ Software and Mechanical Experts


As per my previous update, I confirmed that in a hearing on 10 September, the Court unfortunately did not side with the Claimants
 in respect of the expert applications, and gave some strict directions with regard to steps the parties were required to take in respect of the software evidence that had been prepared.


We have been working hard to prepare and finalise the software report with the redactions / removals as advised by the Court and
 a version of these amended reports was provided to the Defendants on 24 September. We are awaiting the Defendants’ response to this draft report.  


In respect of the Claimants' mechanical expert, the Claimants' barrister team have provided a note to us in which they have flagged
 certain concerns with the mechanical expert. They have raised that they are concerned how the expert will perform at trial and that certain precautions need to be taken with the expert. Importantly, however, they have not told us that these concerns impact
 on the prospects of success of the case and we remain confident in the case we have prepared against Ford.


We are taking this note incredibly seriously and we are working hard, with the other Lead Solicitors, to prepare the expert for
 the trial. We are confident that, even with these concerns, the expert will be suitably prepared for trial, having undergone significant preparatory work before he takes the stand.


The expert is due to travel to the UK, from America, on 29 September, and will largely be based here, with the team, until his
 evidence is complete. He will observe various cross-examinations of other experts and will get a good feel for the experience he is likely to have in the witness box.


The team will also be assisting him in his preparation.


If you have any questions regarding this, please do let me and the Ford team know.


Quantum Trial


As you are aware, the Court has ordered that a second trial be listed in these NOx Litigations for October 2026. This trial, referred
 to as the “Quantum Trial” is in relation to the value of certain claims that are being brought by the Claimants. The Court will assess what value should be attributed to different heads of loss claimed by the Claimants, each of which were sustained as a result
 of the Defendants’ conduct, and determine a value for each claim being brought.


The Quantum Trial is proceeding, at least initially, on the basis of assumptions that the vehicles had prohibited defeat devices
 in them. This is necessary because we will not have a judgment from the Court on the defeat devices until at some point in mid-2026 (post the October 2025 trial), and it is impractical for the entire litigation to grind to a half while waiting for this judgment.
 As such, we will prepare evidence and submissions on what we have pleaded for the PDD Trial, and this will then be updated, in very short order, once we have that judgment.


It is obviously impractical for the Court to hear evidence and consider losses on an individual basis (to do so would defeat the
 purpose of a group litigation), and so how this trial will proceed is by way of Sample Claimants. These are Claimants, selected between the Claimants and Defendants, who represent a range of characteristics and different issues across the Claimant cohort such
 that findings by the Court can be applied to all claimants. The characteristics that the Claimants needed to represent were included in Annex 2 to the October 2024 CMC Order, a copy of which is attached again for ease.


The process of negotiating these Sample Claimants took some time but the parties have finally reach agreement. A total of 40 Sample
 Claimants have been negotiated between the Claimants and Defendants across the Pan-NOx Litigations, split as eight per manufacturer, and of those eight, four selected by the Claimants, and four by the Defendants. Details of the Ford Sample Claimants can be
 provided if required.


Over the course of the negotiations, the Defendants made various nominations that the Claimants wished to resist, for various reasons
 i.e. the Claimants did not wish to participate as Sample Claimants, or they wished to pursue their claim in a different jurisdiction. In circumstances where those Sample Claimant nominees did not wish to proceed, the Defendants have taken the position that
 they must have their claims removed from the English Litigation. We have some sympathy with this, especially where Claimants wish to pursue their claim in a different jurisdiction.


Kenneth Gormley is one such person. Mr Gormley is a Ford Claimant, was nominated by the Defendants as a Sample Claimant, however
 we have since identified he is bringing a claim in both the England & Wales jurisdiction as part of this claim, and also in a separate litigation in Scotland.


Mr Gormley cannot continue with both claims and he was required to pick which one he wanted to continue with and we have instructions
 from Mr Gormley that he wishes to pursue his claim as part of the Scottish proceedings. We therefore are required to prepare and serve a formal notice of discontinuance in respect of Mr Gormley’s claim in the English proceedings.


Pursuant to paragraphs 29 and 30 of the Ford Group Litigation Order, we are seeking your instructions to act on Mr Gormley’s instructions
 and discontinue his claim.


Before confirming these instructions, we must advise you of the effect of this discontinuance. While it will not adversely impact
 the litigation, indeed the Litigation is already proceeding past this, the discontinuance will necessarily result in the Defendants being entitled to incur costs in the Litigation, that will be recoverable by them in due course.


As an initial reassurance, these costs will not be due from you or from any of the Claimants, but they will instead be covered,
 should they need to be paid, by either the ATE provider who is providing cover for this Litigation, or by Mr Gormley himself.


The general rule, under the governing Civil Procedure Rules 38.6 is that where a Claimant discontinues all or part of their claim,
 the Defendant has an automatic right to the costs they have incurred in respect of their claim.


There will be two types of costs that the Defendants will be able to recover: common costs, and individual costs.


As explained in the Client Committee meeting post the first Cost Management Hearing, the individual costs will be costs solely
 in relation to Mr Gormley’s claim, and the common costs will be the apportioned share of the Defendants overall costs of this exercise in relation to Mr Gormley’s claim. Mr Gormley’s claim is one claim out of hundreds of thousands, and so while we remain unaware
 of the level of costs that have been incurred by the Defendants, we believe the overall amount of the common costs will be minimal.


These costs cannot be resolved until the conclusion of the case and so there is no immediate cost that will be required to be paid.


I am of course available to discuss any aspect of this with you before you confirm your instructions, but I wish to reassure you
 that this discontinuance will not result in you, or any of the other thousands of claimants in the Litigation, being out of pocket.


As a result, we respectfully seek your instructions to:


1.      
Proceed to discontinue Mr Gormley’s claim in England & Wales; and

2.      
Remove Mr Gormley from the Ford Group Register.

Please confirm by return that you are content for us to take these steps


Change of Personnel


As a final piece of information, it is with regret that I must inform you that I have made the difficult decision to resign from
 my role at Pogust Goodhead.


I am currently working my notice period, with my final day of employment with the firm still subject to negotiation. As soon as
 I know when my final day is, I will inform you of this. I appreciate you will need to know this information.


Please rest assured that even with me having made the decision to part from the firm, I will be, and I am, continuing to act in
 the best interests of the Claimant Committee, and the wider claimant cohort. I personally have devoted a significant amount of time to this case and I am determined to ensure that the case is as best presented at trial as it can be.


I must also, at this point, advise you that the Partner with overall conduct of the Pan-NOx Litigations for Pogust Goodhead, Peter
 Gallagher, has also resigned. I am unable to comment on the reasons for his departure, but he has formally left the firm and the firm is putting in place a new head of the NOx department. They will contact you to confirm who this person is in due course. 


The remainder of the Ford Pogust Goodhead team remains in situ and they will continue to liaise with you. I remain with conduct
 of the matter, and when a decision has been made as to who will take conduct of the matter once I have departed, I will arrange for a handover to take place such that you are introduced to the new case lead.


Should you have any questions regarding the contents of this letter, please do not hesitate to contact us.


As always, we are grateful for your continued support and attention to the matter.


Yours faithfully,


Michael & the Ford Litigation Team

Michael Burke

As identified in my previous update, the Defendants have made a series of complaints about the expert evidence that we have submitted in the Ford Litigation,
 most specifically the expert evidence of our automotive software engineer, Dr Marcus Heitz. Each of the other Lead Defendants have made similar applications to restrict or reduce the evidence of Dr Heitz.

The Defendants set out their substantive complaints with Dr Heitz's report on 8 August, highlighting almost 50% of his report as being subject to complaint

 retained. This is also the case for the generic material in Mercedes and Dr Tate's evidence. 


 


The Claimants have finalised and served their skeleton argument today and we are in the process of exchanging these with the Defendants. 


 


The hearing is listed for Wednesday, 10 September 2025, and I will update you on the outcome of the hearing later in the week. 


 


If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me to discuss.


 


Kind regards,

STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL


Dear all,


I hope you are all well. I write further to my last update on 29 June 2025, to provide you with an update on the Ford NOx Emissions
 Litigation (the “Ford Litigation”), and the Pan-NOx Litigation generally (the “Litigation”)


As always, please note that the contents and existence of this letter are
strictly privileged and confidential and should not be discussed with anyone other than us, as your legal representative, or other members of the Ford Claimant Committee.


 


In my previous update, I confirmed that we were set for an exceptionally busy July, with three hearings listed (De-designation, Cost Management and a Pre-Trial
 Review), in addition to the exchange of expert reports. I am pleased to say that we have successfully navigated each of those hearings, and exchanged our expert reports, and I set out below a full update in respect of each of those items. 


 


De-designation Hearing
(“DDH”)


 


This DDH took place from 7 - 9 July before Mr Justice Constable and I am pleased to announce that it was a success for the Claimants. The judgment following
 the hearing was released on 25 July 2025 and can be found here: 
https://www.judiciary.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Various-Claimants-v-Mercedes-Benz-Ford-Nissan-Stellantis-and-others.pdf


 


You can also find a helpful summary of the judgment here along with commentary from Pogust Goodhead and Leigh Day:

https://pogustgoodhead.com/dieselgate-high-court-blocks-attempts-by-car-manufacturers-to-hide-key-documents-that-could-show-whether-they-cheated-emissions-tests/


 


In short, the Court ruled that the Manufacturer Defendants cannot hide behind the cloak of confidentiality and must reveal hundreds of documents, including
 the parameters that the vehicles operate within, to the public. The Claimants were entirely justified in their application to lift confidentiality from these documents and the hearing will now be conducted in open court and subject to little or no reporting
 restrictions. There are still some documents that will retain their confidentiality, but it is a small number in comparison to the overall number of documents in the litigations. 


 


This is a significant victory in these cases, including in the Ford case, as it now means the Defendants must now reveal to the world how they calibrate and
 operate their vehicles. It also means that justice will be done publicly and without restriction - something the Defendants fought very hard to maintain. It further increases scrutiny on the Defendants from regulators and other public bodies to ensure that
 they are more closely examined and held to standard.


 


We are presently working on assembling all relevant documents that have previously been provided to you in redacted form, such as the Individual Particulars
 of Claim and we will update the SharePoint accordingly with those unredacted documents. 


 


Cost Management Hearing
(“CMH”)


 


The CMH took place on 15 and 16 July before Mrs Justice Cockerill. The judgment following this hearing has not yet been handed down but we are expecting it
 to be over the course of the summer break and hopefully before September. We will update you as soon as we know more regarding this.


 


Pre-Trial Review (“PTR”)


 


The PTR took place on 28 and 29 July, again before Mrs Justice Cockerill. The Court gave guidance on a number of procedural issues including the expected
 timetable for Trial i.e. what order the cases will be heard in and how long each case will be heard in court, the Trial bundle of documents and protocols governing how the parties are to interact in advance of the hearing. None of this involves any work that
 you as the Claimants need to undertake. 


 


What is of significance however are the two applications that we made to be heard at the PTR in respect of Ford. As forecast in my previous update, we did
 ultimately make an application for Specific Disclosure of certain additional relevant information from Ford. Following sustained negotiations with the Defendants in respect of this, the parties have been able to reach an agreement on certain specific further
 documentation that Ford are to provide us with by 15 August 2025. 


 


Secondly, and importantly, we submitted an application for permission to amend our pleadings. The need for this arose following our review of documents that
 we had received from the Defendants which indicated that there is a defect in certain of the Defendant Vehicles which in turn affects the PDDs that we allege are in the vehicles. Ford are nervous about this information and they sought to oppose this amendment
 to the pleadings. The Court opted to not deal with the application at the PTR but instead to deal with it at a hearing in future, potentially in September.


 


This amendment and bringing the defect to light and into the public will have a significantly positive impact on the case as it bring a host of new pleadings
 against the Defendants. 


 


We will keep you updated on the progress of this application.


 


The other key point the Court dealt with was in relation to expert evidence at the PTR. The Defendants, most notably Ford, have been making a series of on-going
 complaints regarding the contents of our expert reports, stating that they feel the reports go outside the remit of the experts. We of course aver that they do not, instead considering that the Defendants' complaints are instead a cover for their nervousness
 about their contents. Ford in particular have been raising issues regarding the software report that we have filed, primarily we believe because our expert has done an excellent job and presented a very damaging case to Ford that increases the prospects of
 success at trial. 


 


The Court has advised that a further hearing on 10 September will be listed to hear any arguments over the contents of the expert reports, with the parties
 to try and resolve the issues prior to the date of the hearing. We will keep you informed as to this. 


 


Ford Litigation specific matters


 


Expert Reports


 


Per the below update, the initial expert reports have now been exchanged (on the 25 and 27 July respectively) and we are moving towards the third step previously
 advised: the exchange of supplemental expert reports. This is due to occur on the 22nd August. 


 


Our initial review of the expert reports provided by the Defendants is that they do not contain any surprises or give us real cause for concern. Their software
 report is considerably less in-depth than ours, to our advantage, while their mechanical engineer also appears to have struggled to formulate a strong case in Ford's favour. 


 


Claimant Committee Members


 


We are continuing to engage with Virgin Media over their appointment to the Committee and there is no substantive update on this at this point. 


 


Should any of you have any further questions arising out of this update, please do not hesitate to get in contact with me to discuss.


 


Kind regards,

STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL


Dear all,


I hope you are all well. I write further to my last update in May 2025, to provide you with an update on the Ford NOx Emissions
 Litigation (the “Ford Litigation”), and the Pan-NOx Litigation generally (the “Litigation”)


As always, please note that the contents and existence of this letter are
strictly privileged and confidential and should not be discussed with anyone other than us, as your legal representative, or other members of the Ford Claimant Committee.


Having previously updated you on the March and May CMCs, I am pleased to inform you that we have now agreed the resultant Orders
 from those hearings and copies of these are attached.


As you will discern, those Orders do update previous directions, especially the May Order which now sets out a more detailed process
 for disclosure in respect of the Quantum Trial in October 2026,  Details of these updates were contained in my previous update.


As detailed below, the team is currently preparing for a very busy July including three substantive hearings across the month:
 the de-designation hearing, which is listed between 7 - 9 July 2025; a Cost Management Hearing in respect of the Quantum Trial, which is listed between 14 – 16 July 2025; and finally the Pre-Trial Review (the “PTR”) which is listed on 28 and 29 July.


We are also preparing our final expert reports which are due to be exchanged on 16 July 2025, while supplementary reports are to
 be exchanged on 30 July.


In light of the exceptionally busy July, I may be unable to provide you with a substantive update until August, but I will endeavour
 to provide you with any relevant updates following the hearings as required.


Below I set out an update in respect of those three substantive hearings and a general update on the Ford Litigation.


De-designation Hearing
(“DDH”)


One key hurdle the parties face in these Pan-NOx Litigations is that there are significant barriers erected between the Litigations
 that prevent the efficient and effective exchange and comparison of information and disclosure between the cases. This is a fundamental part of the Claimants claim i.e. that many of the manufacturers were either sharing strategies and technology to insert
 prohibits defeat devices (“PDDs”) in their vehicles, or alternatively, that better technology was available that was being used by other manufacturers that mean the Defendants did not need to insert PDDs in their vehicles.


As mentioned in previous updates, much the information that exists in the Ford Litigation, and similarly in the other Lead Cases
 (Mercedes, Renault/Nissan and Peugeot Citroën) is subject to a case specific Confidentiality Ring Orders (“CRO”). Each of the Lead cases has their own CRO. The Defendants have taken this CRO as a means to try and keep secret the majority of the documentation
 that they have provided to us, thereby restricting access to the documents to persons who are members of the CRO. Despite protestations from the Defendants, we have successfully implemented a Pan-Lead CRO, which has been constructed to assist in the sharing
 of confidential information across the cases. While this is helpful in permitted us to see documents from other cases, it does not alleviate the issue of transferring documents into the Pan-Lead CRO (as the Defendants continue to raise various issues regarding
 this) and it does not prevent those documents being confidential and only certain people being able to see them. This does not go to the principle of open justice, whereby the public should know the conduct of these manufacturers. It is and always has been
 our intention to seek to de-designate these documents so that they can be referred to openly and in public.


The DDH is shaped at doing precisely that; bringing those documents into the public and also to make the process of hearing these
 cases in court more feasible. Under present circumstances, any time a party wishes to discuss any documentation that is confidential, it would require the Court room to be emptied of people who are not within the CROs, which is simply unworkable. The DDH is
 intended to allow open justice to be carried out. 


The Claimants prepared and filed their respective applications and witness evidence on 13 June 2025 and we took receipt of the
 Defendants’ responsive evidence late last night. We are considering this with our counsel team in advance of the preparation of skeleton arguments and the hearing itself.


Cost Management Hearing
(“CMH”)


A Cost Management Hearing is scheduled for 14-16 July 2025. The purpose of this hearing is for the parties to agree the costs budgets
 in relation to the Quantum Trial, which is set to take place in October 2026.


You may recall we undertook a similar exercise last July in respect of costs for the PDD Trial, which we are hurtling towards in
 October of this year.


We have instructed the same counsel team as represented us last year which has assisted us in considering the rulings of the Court
 at that hearing. Our budgets were exchanged with the Defendants on 17 June and we have been considering them since. We are due to provide a response to the Defendants budgets in documents knows as Budget Discussion Report (“BDRs”) on 3 July and we are
 working with our counsel team to prepare these now. We image the BDRs may assist in bring about more agreement with the Defendants and in advance of skeleton arguments which are due on 10 July 2025.


Again, we will keep you updated on this hearing as we progress towards it.


Pre-Trial Review (“PTR”)


The final hearing in July and before the summer break is the PTR. Generally this hearing is reserved for procedural matters, including
 timetabling for the main trial, the running order of issues and the trial bundle, as opposed to any more substantive issues between the parties.


However, in these cases which are extraordinary, it is likely that this PTR will deal with a larger number of issues including
 any final applications that the Claimants may wish to make before the Court takes its summer vacation. In the Ford Litigation, we are consider submitting applications for specific documents however we have not yet arrived at the final decision on that point.
  


Preparation for this hearing has already commenced and the teams are identifying issues that they may require to be resolved at
 that hearing.


Again, we will keep you updated on this hearing as we progress towards it.


 


Ford Litigation specific matters


Without Prejudice Meeting –
HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL


A preliminary confidential meeting with Ford took place on 12 June 2025 to discuss the merits of the case. As mentioned in our
 previous update, the aim of this meeting was to inform the Ford Defendants of the strength of our case and seek to narrow the issues between the parties.


In attendance at the meeting were our the Claimant and Defendant counsel teams, as well as some of the Solicitors and Ford also
 sent one of their internal general counsel to attend. During the meeting, the barristers presented a number of key confidential documents to Fords legal team and ventilated a number of high level issues about the case, many of which the Ford became defensive
 about. While the meeting has not yielded any immediate results, from the Claimants' perspective it was positive and we viewed the meeting as having done what it needed to.


We have not yet heard anything further from Ford (which was expected) but we will keep you updated if and when we hear anything
 further from them.


Claimant Committee Members


With your previous consent, we have officially appointed Keith Turner as a new Claimant Committee Member. We are awaiting a signed
 copy of the Claimant Committee Agreement from Virgin Media before they are appointed as a member, and once that is concluded, we will confirm the new Claimant Committee and convene a meeting.


This will likely take place in August. 


Testing


As mentioned in our previous update, the parties have been undergoing tests on all 6 Sample Vehicles. These tests are now concluded,
 and, as expected, the results in many instances have proven to be excellent in assisting the case we are advancing. The results of the testing have been provided to both the Claimant and Defendant experts who are analysing them to incorporate into their reports.


Expert Reports


A crucial step in preparing our case for trial. Our experts (in the fields of automotive software and mechanical engineering) are
 currently preparing reports outlining their analysis of the test results and their findings and opinion regarding PDDs that are contained in Ford vehicles.


This is a 3 step process, the first step having already been concluded.


1.      
A meeting(s) between the experts to formulate a Joint Statement which sets out where the experts opinions align. This has been completed and a copy
 of the report has been added to the SharePoint.

2.      
Exchange of main Expert reports exchanged between the parties . These reports are compiled independent from the other side and represent the individual
 exerts opinions and findings based upon the test results and disclosure. Our experts are working hard to finalise their reports and we are meeting with them regularly to assist them in any way we can.

3.      
Exchange of Supplementary Expert Reports. Once the reports at step 2 above are exchanged, the experts have time to consider the content of those
 reports and then update any opinions in their own report based on what the other expert has said. Work on this will commence immediately after exchange of the reports.

Disclosure and Witness Evidence


As foreshadowed in the previous update, all tranches of disclosure have now been received from the Defendants and a mass review
 exercise is on-going. To date, the Ford Defendants have disclosed approximately 38,000 documents that the combined teams of Pogust Goodhead and Leigh Day are reviewing these to assist in substantiating our case. Some documents include evidence from the Defendants
 showing they had updates available for the vehicles, as they knew they were problematic, however they deigned not to implement them at the time for internal reasons, and other documents show that Ford opted for different strategies in their vehicles in comparison
 to others due to cost considerations.


All of this information is incredibly helpful both for our counsel team who will be presenting the information in court but also
 for our team of experts who will be considering disclosure as part of their report.


We have also taken receipt of a Witness Statement served by Ford from one of their employees who was involved in the development
 of the their diesel engines. They have served this in an effort to rebut our case, however the statement is quite helpful in a number of ways, including alluding to documents which may be damaging to Ford’s case. We and our counsel team are continuing to analyse
 this, and we are engaging with Ford on the document and its contents. It is thought that this individual will attend the trial and he will be cross-examined by our counsel team.


Group Register and Notices of Objection


The official deadline for service of the sixth iteration of the Group Register was on Friday, 20 June 2025.While the Group Register,
 per the terms of the GLO, is due to be served every three months, In light, of the other competing deadlines in the upcoming months, we have agreed with the Defendants to an extension of this deadline to 20 September 2025. We are reviewing our Group Register
 data ahead of the next iteration and will keep you updated.


The Defendants have also provided further objections regarding a small number of claims enrolled in the fourth iteration of the
 Group Register. As they are only able to raise objections in respect of “new” claims enrolled on the Group Register,  or existing claims providing new information, this is a task is diminishing as there are limited “new” claims being entered onto the Group
 Register. In Comparison to previous rounds, the number of objections raised in this time was significantly smaller with the Defendants only objecting to 16 Pogust Goodhead claims, 2 of which are being removed as duplicates. The remaining claims have been either
 rejected or reserved, subject to our clients’ instructions.


I trust this update reassures you that we are continuing to advance at a breakneck pace towards the trial in October 2025 which
 will provide a conclusive outcome to the liability aspect of this matter.


While we are set for an exceptionally busy July, should any of you require anything from me or the Ford team, please let us know.


I hope you all enjoy your summer break and we will be in touch in August.


Kind regards,


 


Michael & the Ford Litigation Team

Team,




Over the last few days post the Lead Solicitor application, I and the other case leads, have been engaging with LD to establish what our
brave new world will look like and how the teams implement it. 




Ultimately, whether we like it or not (and barring the Court going completely left field in their judgment tomorrow), LD are going to be the sole Lead Solicitor on the Ford Litigation. I am genuinely sorry that this has happened and that things have happened
 the way that they have. None of you deserve to the subject to this. This juncture has been reached through no fault of any of yours and believe me when I say I know just how unpleasant it feels. I also fully appreciate that it sucks even more to know that,
 despite how much it feels like we've been relegated to "just another claimant firm", we will still need to perform largely the same role that we have been before now - except we do it without the title of Lead Solicitor.  




As we try to gather some understanding of how this new world will practically work, especially with the Agency Agreement that the firms have executed, there are a few things that look to have been decided that I can inform you of:





The AA (as the firms have executed) puts me under the supervision of LD - it does not extend to you as individuals. You will still work under PG and your day jobs go on as normal. How this works for me and my
 instructions to you, we are all trying to get to the bottom of. You are all smart lawyers and I am sure you can appreciate that I may have some concerns over how this works in practice, but I (and the other case leads) will be doing what we can to a) ensure
 you are fully equipped and supported to do you job and b) find a solution that works for everyone so we can move forward;

LD will take over all comms (incoming and outgoing) to the Ds. As part of the AA that the firms have agreed, I will be CC'ed on those emails, and I will then need to pass them onto the team along with instructions;

Similar with external meetings with the Defendants. The de facto is that LD will attend these solo but there will inevitably be instances where PG team members are needed;

Communications with counsel etc can (I believe) proceed as normal and we shouldn't have to run these past LD, but if that changes, I will let you know;

All external work on the PG SharePoint that is "common work" will at some stage be moved over to the LD SharePoint - this is to ensure links going out to the Ds etc go from a Leigh Day email account (the timeline
 on this is very much TBC becuase of how big of a task it is);

Group Register (and Notice of Objection) work has not yet been decided but §19 of the Ford GLO dictates that PG have responsibility for this, not the Lead Solicitor, so it is likely that this will remain as
 it has been. I will update on this when I know more;

Trial preparation and attendance is expected to be as it would have been otherwise. I have been today working on a rota for who will be where, when. There is also a suggestion that we may work from LD for the
 week(s) before the trial to make preparation and communication easier. This sounds like a very good idea to me and I will update on this when I know more.





It's not all doom and gloom. The entire LD team, especially the LD Ford team and Nichola in particular, know how difficult a time this is for us collectively and all of you as individuals. They are immensely appreciative of all of the work that we are doing
 and they understand that collaboration between us must continue elsewise there is every chance things will fall over. 




We will keep plugging on and I will keep you all as informed as I can over the coming days and weeks. One piece of good news (if you choose to take it as good news) is that I will be in the office almost weekly from now until I depart for my new role, starting
 from next week. We have opening submissions on Monday and Tuesday - let's arrange to do a team lunch, or heaven forbid a drink post-work, one of the days next week to celebrate having got this insanely massive piece of litigation to trial within 2 years of
 making the GLO application - that in itself is insane never mind what we have been through over the last 2 years (and 2 months). I say this often, but I am genuinely astonished at how freakishly competent you all are at your jobs and I am very very proud to
 work alongside all of you. You are all an absolute credit.




As always, I'm around if anyone wants to chat or discuss anything in the email.




Thanks,




Michael

Hi all,




Just in response to the email below re: cost points:



a) Cost of the application for PG stepping down temporarily as Lead Sols on Lead Cases.
Unless I am mistaken, a formal application to amend the GLO should not be required to remove Pogust Goodhead as Lead Solicitors. If all parties agree, this can be dealt with by way of consent order and submitted for court approval prior to the PTR. In that
 scenario, any adverse costs for amending the GLO would be minimal, if any.

If an application has to be made because the Defendants will not agree by consent, then the normal costs consequences apply i.e. costs follow the event. If the Defendants unreasonably refuse, we should not be liable for their adverse costs. If, however, they
 say they will only agree by consent if PG pays their costs incurred since Thursday’s announcement, those costs ought to be minimal. As with any offer for adverse costs, we would need to take client instructions, but the costs exposure can be mitigated if the
 application is made sooner rather than later.



b) Ability to recover common costs as Lead Sols.

Common costs are recoverable inter partes by reference to the approved costs budgets. The default position under each GLO is that Lead Solicitors conduct the common costs work. However, the cost-sharing provisions allow such work to be delegated (with prior
 authorisation) to a Non-Lead Solicitor. This is what has already occurred in Ford, Renault-Nissan, and Citroën-Peugeot with Milberg London LLP.

For example, the Mercedes GLO [43] states:
With the exception of such preparation for and attendance at meetings of the Claimants' Solicitors Group as is reasonably required, no further work in relation to the Common Issues shall be undertaken by any legal representative other than the members of the
 Steering Committee, their servants or agents 
unless authorised in advance by the Steering Committee; and no liability for Common Costs in relation to such work in the absence of such authorisation shall arise between the Claimants or between the parties.

This may therefore require an update to clients to explain that the default position has changed; however, we can also explain the mechanism under the GLO, which permits Non-Lead firms to conduct common work when authorised.



c) CFA deductions.

I do not think the judgment in Julia Mazur v Charles Russell Speechlys LLP [2025] EWHC 2341 (KB) should cause concern. Paralegal work is recoverable in costs provided that:

(a) it does not involve conducting “reserved legal activities” independently;
(b) it is supervised by an authorised individual; and
(c) it is reasonable and proportionate in nature and amount.

None of our paralegals conduct reserved legal activities within the meaning of section 12(1) of the Legal Services Act 2007. These activities are limited to:



the exercise of a right of audience;


the conduct of litigation (issuing a claim form, signing statements of truth, filing a defence/response, etc.);


reserved instrument activities (e.g. drafting a transfer of land, completing registration documents for the Land Registry);


probate activities;


notarial activities; or


administration of oaths.


Accordingly, PG stepping down as Lead Solicitors does not prevent the firm from being instructed under the GLO to conduct common work and does not impact the level of CFA deductions that may be applied to client damages.

Dear Raminder,


Thank you for coming back to me and for accepting my resignation. My apologies for the delay in coming back to you,
 as I’m sure you are aware there are a lot of things in the air!


Noting your comments regarding my resignation being premature, I disagree with that assessment, but we are where we

 I'm more than happy to do so. 


This email is in two parts: i) to address my notice period and when may be a good time for me to depart the firm;
 and ii) to address on-going travel and litigation needs with a view to finding a pragmatic way to handle future travel etc.


Notice Period


I agree that we need to work collaboratively to find an appropriate point for me to leave the firm, both to ensure
 the clients are protected and not disadvantaged, and to ensure that I am protected and not prejudiced. My current leave date is I understand the 15 December 2025. There are various important deadlines between now and then an to add a little more colour to
 those deadlines, the deadlines we have approaching (demarcated as PDD or Quantum) are as follows:



06.10.2025 – PTR 2 (PDD)
10.10.2025 – receipt of disclosure from Defendants (Quantum)
13.10.2025 – Trial starts (PDD)
21.11.2025 – Individual Particulars of Quantum to be filed and served (Quantum)
11.12.2025 – receipt of disclosure from Defendants (Quantum)
19.12.2025 – Trial ends (PDD)



19.12.2025 – Applications for January 2026 CMC (Quantum)




As is evident, the litigation has a large number of critical deadlines looming. Overlayed with this, is the added complication of each OEM having its own CRO, as well as an overall
 Pan-NOx CRO.


Each individual must apply to the Defendants (individually per CRO and to all Defendants for the Pan-Lead CRO) for
 permission to be entered into that CRO. This takes up to 5 working days. There is also a process for applying to be removed from each CRO which can, in itself, take some days.


Given the level of confidential information in the NOx litigations, someone who is not in one, or all, of the CROs,
 is necessarily extremely limited as to what they can see, do and work on. For example, they could not actively participate in the trial, nor could they provide any type of meaningful input into any of the directions that fall across the period that they are
 not in the CRO i.e. the IPQs. If therefore I am held to work my notice until 15 December, I will be unable to attend trial for the final week before Christmas, nor will I will be able to really assist with any work on quantum disclosure, or work on the applications
 / witness statements for the January 2026 CMC.


Considering this, we (both me and Pogust Goodhead) need to realistically consider when my departure should fall, as
 it should come at a time that will be at the least detriment of the claimants.


To that end, it seems sensible, and would be in everyone’s interests, for me to depart Pogust Goodhead on a date that
 will allow me to start my new role and be re-entered into the various CROs, which does not conflict with any of those deadlines, nor run over a critical part of the trial that I am intended to participate in. To require me to serve my notice such that I leave
 the firm on a date which conflicts with a major deadline would be of significant detriment to the clients, not only of this firm, but to other firms as well.


Having considered the timetable and what is genuinely in the best interests of everyone, especially the clients, it
 would appear the best date for me to depart Pogust Goodhead is the 17 October. This date falls after the opening submissions, and across the Normal Driving Conditions expert evidence (which is plainly of importance, but falls at the lower end of the scale
 of importance considering the other critical tasks over the trial period). Exiting Pogust Goodhead then, will allow me sufficient time to commence my new role before substantive evidence relating to the manufacturers starts.

 will have a negative impact on the claimants. For a Partner with current conduct of an ALGLO, who has detailed knowledge of all of the cases across the Pan-NOx Litigation, to be unable to participate in the trial, is not in anyone’s interests. The obvious

Future Travel

Notice Period

 the clients are protected and not disadvantaged, and to ensure that I am protected and not prejudiced. My current leave date is I understand the 15 December 2025. There are various important deadlines between now and then an to add a little more colour to
 those deadlines, the deadlines we have approaching (demarcated as PDD or Quantum) are as follows:



06.10.2025 – PTR 2 (PDD)
10.10.2025 – receipt of disclosure from Defendants (Quantum)
13.10.2025 – Trial starts (PDD)
21.11.2025 – Individual Particulars of Quantum to be filed and served (Quantum)
11.12.2025 – receipt of disclosure from Defendants (Quantum)
19.12.2025 – Trial ends (PDD)



19.12.2025 – Applications for January 2026 CMC (Quantum)



As is evident, the litigation has a large number of critical deadlines looming. Overlayed with this, is the added
 complication of each OEM having its own CRO, as well as an overall Pan-NOx CRO.


Each individual must apply to the Defendants (individually per CRO and to all Defendants for the Pan-Lead CRO)
 for permission to be entered into that CRO. This takes up to 5 working days. There is also a process for applying to be removed from each CRO which can, in itself, take some days.


Given the level of confidential information in the NOx litigations, someone who is not in one, or all, of the
 CROs, is necessarily extremely limited as to what they can see, do and work on. For example, they could not actively participate in the trial, nor could they provide any type of meaningful input into any of the directions that fall across the period that they
 are not in the CRO i.e. the IPQs. If therefore I am held to work my notice until 15 December, I will be unable to attend trial for the final week before Christmas, nor will I will be able to really assist with any work on quantum disclosure, or work on the
 applications / witness statements for the January 2026 CMC.

 as it should come at a time that will be at the least detriment of the claimants.

 that will allow me to start my new role and be re-entered into the various CROs, which does not conflict with any of those deadlines, nor run over a critical part of the trial that I am intended to participate in. To require me to serve my notice such that
 I leave the firm on a date which conflicts with a major deadline would be of significant detriment to the clients, not only of this firm, but to other firms as well.

 it would appear the best date for me to depart Pogust Goodhead is the 17 October. This date falls after the opening submissions, and across the Normal Driving Conditions expert evidence (which is plainly of importance, but falls at the lower end of the scale
 of importance considering the other critical tasks over the trial period). Exiting Pogust Goodhead then, will allow me sufficient time to commence my new role before substantive evidence relating to the manufacturers starts.

 itself gets used for something else at the last minute; andGiven the trial starts in October with summer in between, I anticipate at least some of the trial prep costs will be incurred before the end of July. I
